newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds hard pressed to rally more.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds hard pressed to rally more.

text.p: *Australian bonds are finding difficulty continuing the current uptrend in the absence of any major local data, and will be vulnerable to movements in U.S. Treasuries for now.
*However, further forward, the outlook remains positive.

Australian bonds are finding difficulty in following through the current advance with no major economic data due until next week, and even then the focus will be more on inflation and wages reports at end-October.
Ten-year bond yields got to their lowest level at around 7.75 percent in early trading, following on from a rally in U.S. Treasuries, but lacked the momentum to carry on, traders said.
"It's largely been day traders moving the market around. For now I think we are confined to watching the wobbles of the U.S. market," one trader at a local bank said.
U.S. bonds extended the post-FOMC rally on Wednesday as the market attracted demand after the Fed's unchanged policy stance.
However, the domestic market's lack of self-motivation is likely to be short-lived.

"Our forecast is that the long bond (yield) can get down to 7.50, 7.25 percent on a three to six month view, and that's assuming another rate cut," said Rory Robertson, fixed interest analyst at Bankers Trust Australia.
"A rate cut is not a done deal. We basically need some good prices and wages data on October 23 and 24," he added.
Robertson, and many other analysts, are predicting a cut in current 7.0 percent interest rates in November.
The December bill futures contract is already discounting an easing of over 25 basis points by maturity, closing at 93.36, the equivalent of a cash rate of 6.64 percent.
The initial rally saw December 10-year bond futures contract take out the August peak of 92.210, touching a high of 92.240.

"I think Aussie bonds are due for a minor correction and down to about 92.070," said Mark Power, technical analyst at MMS Standard & Poor's. "I think they will resume the upside after that...moving back to 92.250 again and then up to 92.500."

The local market's inability to push further ahead saw it slightly underperform U.S. and Canadian debt markets. The 10-year spread to the U.S. had touched a two-year low of 104 basis points briefly on Wednesday.

The 10-year bond slipped through 92.210, but should find some support at 92.110 and again at 92.070. The latter would fill the chart gap left over from Wednesday's spike in prices which followed the FOMC meeting.
